note: Rewritten to the corpus-wide (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) convention. Mistral read the page correctly here — the glyph really is a circled letter — but U+24D0 is a presentation form the rest of the corpus never uses: Hefferon, Grinstead & Snell and Calculus Vol. 3 all print part-labels as (a) or a., and the splitter and distributor match on that. Leaving the circled form in would make the label set inconsistent with every other book in the dataset.
